source.title: Natively Unlearnable Large Language Models
source.authors: Gaurav R. Ghosal; Pratyush Maini; Aditi Raghunathan

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests a native unlearning method against prompting and fine-tuning attacks, and finds that it resists them at least in the Harry Potter case study, while a post-hoc NPO baseline is rapidly reversed by fine-tuning.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own results for NULLs, post-hoc gradient-unlearning baselines, prompting attacks, and fine-tuning attacks. It also cites prior work on quantization and other attacks; those cited results are not recorded as rows. Hyperparameter values and source-mask design choices are not outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own attacks on unlearned models. It fine-tunes an NPO-unlearned 1B transformer on a subset of Harry Potter text and finds it reversed within 10 steps, which bears on B and on A. It also tests a new native-unlearning method (NULLs) against GCG prompting and subset relearning, which bears on F. It is not one of the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that NULLs isolates source-specific knowledge while preserving shared knowledge and general capability, matching retraining. They also conclude that disabling the sink resists GCG extraction and relearning, matching a never-trained model, whereas post-hoc NPO degrades related knowledge and is reversed within about 10 fine-tuning steps.
record.recipe_differences: NULLs is trained from scratch with shared backbone neurons and source-specific sparse sink masks; unlearning disables a source mask rather than applying a post-hoc gradient update. The paper also evaluates NPO and gradient ascent as baselines.
record.method_sensitivity: For Wikipedia, increasing sink-mask overlap slightly widens the gap between Sink-Off and retraining, while increasing active sinks per source has no consistent effect on Sink-Off Truth Ratio. The study reports that sink-pool size and overlap affect memorization and leakage.
record.problems: The experiments use 1B-parameter models and only two source definitions. Prompting and relearning robustness are tested in the Harry Potter case study only. Many plotted comparisons are described without numerical values in the text, so their exact effect sizes cannot be recorded.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on the claim were omitted. The supplementary generation examples in Appendix A.1/Table 4 are not separately rowed because they repeat the qualitative Sink-On versus Sink-Off generation comparison in Figure 6.

untested.parts: Near-chance accuracy on targeted knowledge for post-hoc methods is not reported numerically. Prompting and quantization attacks are not run on post-hoc models. There is no WMDP-style hazardous-knowledge setting.
Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data; other post-hoc methods besides NPO; models larger than 1B.
Entirely untested. There is no direction ablation or access-vs-deletion analysis of post-hoc-unlearned models. NULLs' sink toggling is by design, not a recovery attack.
Quantization is not tested (only cited, Zhang et al. 2025).
No prompting attacks (rephrasing, GCG, other languages, in-context) are run on post-hoc-unlearned models.

Quantization, jailbreaks other than GCG, other languages and in-context attacks are untested. Robustness is tested only in the Harry Potter case at 1B. The permanent weight-zeroing mode is not evaluated.

missing.what: Sink-Off vs Retrained truth ratio as the overlap ratio varies (leakage grows with overlap), and as Nsource varies (no consistent effect on Sink-Off)
Mean article-specific truth ratio of NULLs vs standard transformer (knowledge capacity)

record.verdict_notes: Most results are figure-only. NULLs results bear on F (the counter-method), not on A, C or E, which concern conventional unlearning. The study's evidence on shallow post-hoc unlearning comes from R14 (B, A) and R7/R9 (A collateral damage). Sink-Off routes to the next-closest source's sink rather than deleting weights.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test whether all current post-hoc unlearning methods meet the stated combination of near-chance targeted performance, preserved general ability, and attack resistance. General benchmark scores are reported for NULLs versus a standard transformer, not explicitly for every unlearned checkpoint.
Fine-tuning is tested on a subset of Harry Potter book text, not on unrelated or loosely related examples or a subset of forgotten facts in other settings.
The paper does not test ablating an activation direction in post-hoc-unlearned models. Its access-versus-deletion evidence concerns NULLs' source-specific sinks.
The study tests Cloze-style questions and GCG-optimized adversarial prompts, but not other languages, jailbreak methods beyond GCG, or in-context information.
Robustness is tested for NULLs in the Harry Potter case study against adversarial prompting and fine-tuning; the study does not test resistance to quantization or all listed attack types.

relation.reason: The study runs its own GCG and relearning attacks on NULLs and a relearning attack on an NPO baseline.

tranche.reason: NULLs is a different method (train-time source sinks) aimed at the same question. The study's own NPO relearning and GA/NPO selectivity results are T5-like comparators, but T2 fits the main contribution.

source_check.notes: Nearly all NULLs results are figure-only, except Table 1 and the R18 qualitative text. The text names neither the host model for the Wikipedia NPO/GA runs nor the size of the HP standard transformer, and gives no NPO settings. R14's single state is relative to B; for A the attack succeeds. The authors say Table 1 matches within one SD, but Winogrande (0.530 vs 0.510) does not. Fig 8a (overlap ratio) has no row and should be added as missing.

statements.problem: No error. The text states the result in Sec 4.1.2 but gives no numbers, so 'figure only' is accurate for the values. The study reports no general-capability measure for the NPO or GA models.

statements.correction: R14: NPO-unlearned standard transformer (Harry Potter setting, C4 + 7 HP books; size not stated, case-study models are 1B). Fine-tuning on a reserved HP subset sharply lowers held-out loss, reversing NPO within 10 steps (Fig 7b, figure only). NULLs Sink-Off matches the Retrained model's relearning curve. Measure is loss, not accuracy; no WMDP.
statements.problem: This study has no WMDP result and no forget-example count. The conditions line cites it as 'a 1B NULLs model', but the result bearing on B (R14) is NPO on a standard transformer. The NULLs model showed no excess relearning.

statements.correction: NULLs (1B, trained from scratch on Wikipedia or on C4 + 7 HP books; source-specific sparse sink masks disabled at inference). Sink-Off matches Retrained on article-specific/unique-fact truth ratio (Figs 3b, 4) and on HP loss and Cloze truth ratio (Fig 5). GCG ACR is comparable to Retrained (Fig 7a). Fine-tuning on a reserved HP subset matches Retrained relearning (Fig 7b). Table 1, NULLs vs standard transformer: ARC-E 0.428 vs 0.434, Winogrande 0.530 vs 0.510. All results are figure-only except Table 1.
statements.problem: The statement cites R1, R3, R11, R12, R13, R16, R19 and R20 but never describes this study. The method list leaves out NULLs (train-time source sink masks), and 'Attacks are full-parameter fine-tuning' leaves out the GCG attack (R12).
